description: FAKE reference vectors for mycarlos-send/1 (patient to clinic), DRAFT for review. No signature, key, cipher or randomness is used: signing inputs are bytes, and every hash below is over fixed FAKE bytes. Not a conformance claim for any real component.
canonical_json: sorted keys, no spaces, UTF-8, strings and integers and null only (RFC 8785 for these objects)
frame: each part preceded by its length as eight bytes, big endian
compact_form: b64url(payload).b64url(signature), unpadded; the signature covers signing_input(kind, payload) = frame(domain, payload), never the base64 text; a verifier requires canonical(parse(payload)) == payload before anything else

definition.attachment_head: the link after the last chunk
definition.message_head: sha256(frame('mycarlos-send/1 message', message_id16, sha256(sealed_envelope), head_of_attachment_0, head_of_attachment_1, ...))
definition.who_checks: the portal recomputes every head from the ciphertext it holds (it can: attachment_id is in the outer record), which finds corruption and loss; it does NOT protect against the portal, which can recompute anything. The protective check is CARLOS's: after opening, the chain heads named inside the SIGNED envelope must equal the heads it recomputes from what it fetched

queued.means: kept in the sent record; nothing has been sent yet

sending.means: parts are being uploaded in this run of the app
sending.never_means: that the portal has all of it

received.means: the portal says it holds every part and that the chain it can recompute matches
received.never_means: that the clinic has it, or that the portal's check protects against the portal

collected.means: the clinic's system fetched, opened and checked the message
collected.never_means: filed, seen or read by anyone

filed.means: stored in the clinic's pending-review queue for staff, not yet in a chart
filed.never_means: that any staff member has read, reviewed or acted on it

refused.by: clinic-signed, or portal-claim before the clinic collected it
refused.means: not accepted, for one reason from a fixed list; nothing is kept

expired.by: portal-claim or app, only before the clinic collected it
expired.means: the time ran out before the clinic's system collected it; the portal deleted it
expired.never_means: that it was delivered; after a signed collected only the clinic's signed answer ends the message

recalled.means: removed from the pending queue before it was accepted into a chart

cancelled.by: app and portal, before the upload was completed
cancelled.means: the upload was stopped and everything deleted
cancelled.never_means: anything about a message that was completed

rules.after_a_signed_collected: only the clinic's signed filed, refused or recalled ends the message; the portal's unsigned refused or expired is shown as 'the portal says ...' and changes nothing; the clinic's system enforces expires_at itself (a signed refused with reason expired)
rules.cancel_vs_complete: one row lock on the message: the first wins; a cancel after complete is 409 use_recall, a complete after cancel is 409 cancelled
rules.recall_vs_accept: the clinic's recall handling and its accept-into-chart take the same row lock on the inbound row: the first wins and the loser reads the other's result (recalled, or recall_refused with reason recall_too_late)
rules.recall: a recall is a device-signed object (message_id, chain_head, clinic_id); the portal relays it, the clinic verifies the signature against its accepted-device table and the chain head against its own record, then answers with a signed recalled or recall_refused
rules.interrupted_send: the content key lives only in memory: a restart, a lock or a crash ends the send. The app cancels what the portal holds and the patient sends again as a NEW message_id, so a nonce is never used twice under one key
